title: A quick end-of-month budget check before October starts
dek: September ends tomorrow, and a ten-minute look at your accounts tonight can help you start October without surprises.
body: Tomorrow is the last day of September, which means a lot of bills, renewals and autopays are about to reset for a new month. Before bed tonight, it can help to spend about ten minutes looking at where the money went this month.

It works best when it stays simple. Open your bank app and scroll through the month once. Look for three things: any charge you do not recognize, any subscription you forgot you had, and any category that got bigger than you expected. There is no need to judge yourself while you do it. Just notice.

Many people find something small. It might be a streaming service picked up to watch one show, or a free trial that quietly turned into a paid plan. Canceling one of those before the new billing cycle can feel like finding a few dollars in a coat pocket.

It is also worth checking which bills come out in the first week of October. For a lot of households, rent and utilities land right at the start of the month, and knowing the dates ahead of time keeps you from spending money that is already spoken for. If a charge looks wrong, your bank or card issuer is the right place to ask.
Tonight, pick one subscription or recurring charge and ask yourself if you would sign up for it again today. If the answer is no, cancel it before October begins.
